newsitem.title: USA: Greenbrier sees leasing unit deal accretive.
newsitem.headline: Greenbrier sees leasing unit deal accretive.

text.p: Greenbrier Cos Inc said Wednesday it had bought out a minority stake held in its leasing unit for $16 million, and increased its stake in its TrentonWorks subsidiary by 10 percent to 61 percent.

The company said its purchase of Chrysler Financial Corp's stake in the Greenbrier Capital trailer and container leasing unit was expected to be accretive to earnings by about $0.05 per share in the 1997 fiscal year.
On an annualized basis, the company said, the deal would be accretive to earnings by $0.06 to $0.07 per share.

"Greenbrier Capital has been very active in remarketing and leasing its fleet over the past 18 months," President and Chief Executive William Furman said in a statement. "This has mitigated much of the need for a risk-sharing minority partner with an equity type of return which greatly exceeds our current cost of borrowed funds."
Greenbrier did not say how much it paid to increase its interest in TrentonWorks.
